clue.text: Alcoholic drinking Pepsi sadly, most sentimental

indicators.note: the drunkard 'drinking' something takes it inside, so the scrambled soft drink goes within the other piece

parts.note: an alcoholic is a sot, a habitual drunkard

indicators.note: sadly signals that the brand name is in a bad state, its letters disordered

explanation.surface: A drunk morosely knocking back cola gets maudlin and soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals the anagram and 'drinking' the containment; Pepsi is a soft drink, so the alcoholic in the surface is drinking cola.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy means mawkishly sentimental, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: See 25
One drink or two taking effect on blue fluid

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: to effect something is to bring it about, to do it

indicators.note: fluid means shifting and unfixed, so the colour's letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A barfly orders a second drink and starts feeling the blues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' rearranges BLUE to UBLE, placed under DO; 'taking' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a twofold measure of spirits: one drink that counts as two.

clue.text: Framework I see in coffee

indicators.note: the I and the see-letter sit in the coffee, placed inside its letters

parts.note: a latte is a milky espresso coffee
C is a sound-alike stand-in letter for see

explanation.surface: Someone peering into their coffee spots a structure in the foam.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is an open criss-cross structure of strips, a kind of framework.

clue.text: Pottery, a jar cut in isinglass

indicators.note: the shortened jar piece is placed in the mineral, inside its letters

parts.note: isinglass is an old name for mica, the mineral in thin transparent sheets

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter, trimmed short

parts.note: a jar is a jolt, a sudden jarring shock

explanation.surface: A potter's jar is packed in sheets of isinglass for safe keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' is not a vessel but a jolt; 'cut' removes its last letter, and 'in' places the result inside the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is tin-glazed Italian earthenware, a type of decorated pottery.

clue.text: A singing bear going after port — uproar!

indicators.note: the bear and the A come after the port in the answer

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England
Baloo is the bear who sings 'The Bare Necessities' in Disney's The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A crooning bear chasing after the drink port causes a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine in this drink-filled puzzle, but it is the English port of Hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a noisy commotion, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: Those seven sailed, one short, one of four

parts.note: the seven seas are what sailors proverbially sail

indicators.note: short means the number word is cut back by a letter at its end

explanation.surface: Seven sailors set off, one fewer than a full crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one short' does not mean one fewer sailor: 'short' cuts the number word itself. The final 'one of four' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring, summer, autumn and winter are the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Drink in a pub not entirely cold sent back by military commander

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

indicators.note: sent back has the words after the commander read in reverse
not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a local is your neighbourhood pub
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: An officer sends back a drink at the pub because it's not cold enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' removes the last letter of the pub word, and 'sent back' reverses the whole run A + LOCA + C. 'in' and 'by' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca-Cola is a soft drink brand, the classic fizzy cola.

clue.text: Delight in the morning milk

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon
to milk something is to exploit it, make use of it

explanation.surface: The joy of fresh milk delivered early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' is a verb meaning exploit, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to entertain or please them, a verb sense shared with amuse.

clue.text: Weapon observed during the peepshow

indicators.note: during says the letters run through the middle of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A weapon was spotted while someone watched a seedy peepshow.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a fencing sword, the weapon used in one of the three fencing disciplines.

clue.text: Very deep saying recalled, amid praise

indicators.note: amid puts the turned-round saying in the middle of the praise word

parts.note: to bless God is to praise Him

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, has the word run backwards

parts.note: a motto is a short saying

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a profound proverb while giving thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like plain remembering, but it means called back, so the saying runs in reverse; 'amid' places it inside the praise word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a bottom seems to go down forever, so it is extremely deep.

clue.text: One's emptied volume into river, the entire works

indicators.note: emptied takes out everything between the first and last letters
the volume letter goes into the river name, inside it

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
V is the symbol for volume

explanation.surface: Someone empties a book into a river, along with all their works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is One is: 'emptied' leaves OE. The Ure is a North Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's oeuvre is their complete body of work, everything they produced.

clue.text: Loud, very boisterous of course, one must be restrained

indicators.note: the restrained letter is held in, kept inside the jumbled letters
boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so the phrase's letters run riot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd has to be held back, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boisterous' rearranges OF COURSE, and 'must be restrained' holds I inside that, making OCIFEROUS after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vociferous means noisy and clamorous, shouting forcefully.

clue.text: Member, in being welcomed by leaders in Chinese government, on the up

indicators.note: welcomed by means the earlier pieces are taken in between the two leading letters
leaders in means the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body, an arm or leg

explanation.surface: A new member of the Chinese government is warmly received and rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' only links. 'welcomed by' puts the member and 'in' between the two first letters picked by 'leaders in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing means ascending, going higher, which is what being on the up describes.

clue.text: Infatuated with food, boy guzzles

indicators.note: the boy who guzzles takes the food inside himself

parts.note: a son is a boy
tuck is British school slang for sweets and snacks

explanation.surface: A greedy lad gobbling his snacks is besotted with food.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British slang for food, as in a school tuck shop. 'guzzles' puts it inside the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stuck on someone is an idiom for being keen on or smitten with them.

clue.text: In middle of moss, fish eating finest molluscs

indicators.note: In places the fish piece in between the two central letters
middle of takes the central letters of the word
the fish eating something takes it inside

parts.note: a cod is a fish
top means best, the finest

explanation.surface: A fish nestled in moss is feeding on the best of the shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers: 'eating' puts the finest inside the fish, then 'In' puts that between the middle letters of moss.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopods are eight-armed cephalopods such as the octopus, a group of molluscs.

clue.text: Within walls of park, a bitter brought over for one of those on the gate?

definitions.text: one of those on the gate?

indicators.note: Within places the next pieces between the outer letters
the walls of a word are its first and last letters
brought over has the word turned round, read backwards

parts.note: bitter weather is very cold

explanation.surface: A pint of bitter is carried across the park to drinkers at the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' is chill weather, not beer. 'brought over' turns it round, and 'Within' places A plus that between the park's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A padlock is the removable lock hung on a gate; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Notes produced by this wine to drink at home

indicators.note: the wine is to drink the home piece, taking it inside

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means at home

explanation.surface: Tasting notes for a wine to enjoy at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests tasting notes; it is musical notes. 'to drink' puts the home word inside the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, the source of the musical notes.

clue.text: Behind the door of condominium, indulgence ultimately swell

parts.note: being behind the door means being inside, in
a condominium is an apartment, a flat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Indulging inside your apartment eventually makes you bloat.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate is to blow up and get bigger, which is to swell.

clue.text: Drinking stout, the highlight of sainthood Brendan finally put on some weight!

indicators.note: put on places the last letter on after what goes before
drinking means the stout piece is taken inside the saintly ring

parts.note: a halo is the ring of light shown around a saint
stout means fat, as an adjective, not the dark beer

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Saint Brendan, sipping stout, ends up gaining pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' is the adjective for portly, not the beer. 'Drinking' puts it inside the saint's ring of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Half a ton is a quantity of mass, a measure of weight in tons.

clue.text: Drink fizzy pop in Levantine city

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

indicators.note: fizzy means bubbling, so the word's letters bubble into a new order

explanation.surface: Fizzy drinks are on sale in a city of the Levant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' rearranges POP to PPO; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a historic city in northern Syria, in the region called the Levant.

clue.text: Drug for case of zoophobia, heading for cage

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters, the casing
heading for takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A medication for someone scared of animals, before they go into the cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is a brand of fluoxetine, an antidepressant medication.

clue.text: Curdled drink, sweetener served up like jelly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a sop is a sweetener, something given to placate
jelly that is set has firmed up

explanation.surface: A sugary curdled drink is served wobbling like a jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetener' is a placating offering, SOP, not sugar; 'served up' turns it to POS.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset is a hot drink of milk curdled with ale or wine.

clue.text: City, capital city, one becoming nothing in endless chaos

indicators.note: the changed capital sits in the shortened chaos word
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mess is chaos

indicators.note: becoming signals one letter turning into another

parts.note: Tripoli is the capital of Libya
I is the Roman numeral one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A city whose capital has descended into ruin and disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' changes the first one-letter into a nothing-letter in the Libyan capital; 'endless' drops the last letter of the chaos word, and 'in' puts the changed capital inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large, important city.

clue.text: Scotch is a weapon

definitions.meaning: to scotch a plan is to thwart it

explanation.surface: Whisky as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like the whisky; it is the verb meaning put a stop to.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a plan is to thwart it, and a foil is a fencing sword.

clue.text: Colours of spectral phenomena fading, each one's ending

indicators.note: each one's ending takes the final letter of every word in the list

explanation.surface: The hues of ghostly apparitions are fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's colours are its flag, the banner it carries.

clue.text: It's rich to serve rum and coke up!

indicators.note: to serve rum, read as to make something odd, says the words after it are served up in a strange order

explanation.surface: A bartender's call to pour rum and cola for a rich customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the spirit, but it is the British adjective for odd. 'to serve rum' tells you to arrange AND COKE UP oddly; 'up' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound cake is a dense, buttery cake, traditionally made with a pound each of butter, sugar, flour and eggs, so it is notably rich.

clue.text: One beyond twelve brewing green tea

indicators.note: brewing has the tea's letters stewing into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone older than twelve makes a pot of green tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is aged thirteen to nineteen, so past the age of twelve.
